metadata.name: Qatar Central Bank Technology Risks Circular
metadata.description: Mandatory cyber security and technology risk regulation issued by the Qatar Central Bank (QCB) for all banks operating in the State of Qatar. Sets governance, operational, enterprise security, and business application controls that banks must implement and attest compliance to annually.
metadata.classification_reasoning: Issued as a mandatory circular by Qatar Central Bank for the State of Qatar's banking sector. Banks are required to comply, perform annual compliance assessments, and report material gaps to QCB. QCB reserves the right to audit at any point.
metadata.framework_purpose: To provide guidance to bank users, employees, contractors and other authorized users of their obligatory requirements for protecting the technology and information assets of the bank, and to ensure alignment of bank cyber security frameworks with the requirements of the circular.
metadata.framework_scope: All banks operating in the State of Qatar; covers bank users, employees, contractors, third parties and any authorized users; spans governance, HR, legal/compliance, procurement, risk, BCM, IT operations, enterprise security, and business applications.
framework_objectives: Establish a cyber security function and framework approved by the board
Implement organisational, technical, and procedural controls to protect information assets
Ensure resilience and recoverability of banking operations against cyber threats
Govern third-party, outsourcing, and data-center risk
Prevent and detect internal and external fraud across all banking channels
Comply with QCB reporting and annual compliance assessment requirements
metadata.target_audience: Boards, senior management, CISOs, IT Heads, Risk Management, Legal & Compliance, HR, Procurement, BCM, Internal Audit, and operations teams of banks operating in Qatar
certification_lifecycle: Board-Signed Compliance Report Submission to QCB
metadata.penalty_for_non_compliance: Non-compliance is reviewed by QCB; material gaps must be remediated under board oversight. QCB may audit at any point and may impose supervisory measures consistent with its supervision and control authority.
adoption_approach: Establish a board-approved cyber security framework and CISO function
Conduct gap assessment against this circular
Implement controls across governance, HR, legal, procurement, risk, BCM, IT operations, enterprise security, and business applications
Perform at least annual compliance assessment and board sign-off
Submit compliance report to QCB; remediate material gaps with documented action plan
Subject the bank's information systems to at least annual audit covering infrastructure, people, and processes

controls.title: Establish board-approved cyber security function and framework
controls.description: The bank shall ensure that a cyber security function and framework are established and approved by the board/board authorized committee.
controls.full_text: The bank shall ensure that a cyber security function (team, committee, etc.) and framework are established. These shall be approved by the board/board authorized committee.
evidence_requirements: Board/committee minutes approving the cyber security framework
Organisational chart showing the cyber security function

controls.title: Annual senior-management review of controls
controls.description: The board shall request senior management to periodically review the adequacy of cyber security controls at least annually.
controls.full_text: The board shall request the senior management to periodically review (at least annually) the adequacy of cyber security controls in line with the emerging cyber threats. Senior management shall provide reasonable justification to the board for any identified material gaps.
evidence_requirements: Annual review report to the board
Threat-landscape briefings reviewed by the board

controls.title: Board oversight, risk appetite, and technical representation
controls.description: Board must oversee technology/cyber risks, approve an overall cyber risk appetite and have adequate technical representation.
controls.full_text: The board must have oversight of technology and cyber security risks, and ensure that measures are in place to support their business strategies and objectives. The board must approve an overall cyber risk appetite. Risk appetite is the defined level of risk that may be accepted by the bank. The board must have adequate technical representation to guide them on matters pertaining to cyber security. These technical representative members shall have adequate experience in cyber security or must be experts in cyber security.
evidence_requirements: Board member CVs evidencing cyber expertise

controls.title: Board-approved cyber security policy
controls.description: Board must approve a cyber security policy to manage security risks and safeguard information assets.
controls.full_text: The board must approve a cyber security policy to manage security risks and safeguard information assets.

controls.title: Board-approved cyber strategy and budget with contingency
controls.description: Board must approve the overall cyber security strategy and budget, including built-in contingency considerations.
controls.full_text: The board must approve the overall cyber security strategy and budget. The budget must contain built in contingency considerations.
evidence_requirements: Annual cyber security budget with contingency line items

controls.title: Cyber security function with cross-functional representation
controls.description: Board shall put in place a cyber/information security function with representation from IT, banking technology, risk, security, HR, BCM, legal and compliance.
controls.full_text: The board shall put in place, a cyber security/information security function for effective implementation of cyber security controls. It shall have adequate representation from relevant departments such as IT, banking technology, risk, information security, human resources (HR), business continuity, legal and compliance.

controls.title: Annual review of policies, standards and procedures
controls.description: Cyber security policies, standards and procedures must be updated and reviewed at least annually.
controls.full_text: Cyber security policies, standards and procedures must be updated and reviewed at least on an annual basis.

controls.title: Board oversight of technology risk and IT committees
controls.description: Board and senior management shall oversee technology risks, establish IT policies/standards/procedures, and form IT strategy, IT steering and technology risk committees.
controls.full_text: The board and senior management shall have oversight of technology risks and ensure that the organization's IT function (team, committee, etc.) is capable of supporting its business strategies and objectives. The bank must establish IT policies, standards and procedures, which are critical components of the framework, to manage technology risks and safeguard information system assets in the organization. The bank shall form committees that oversee IT Strategy, IT Steering and technology risk management.
controls.category: Cyber security policy and the organization
evidence_requirements: IT policy, standard and procedure register
IT Strategy/IT Steering/Technology Risk committee charters

controls.title: Cyber/information security organisation and programme
controls.description: Bank shall put in place a cyber/information security organisation responsible for designing, establishing, operating and improving the security program in line with leading practices.
controls.full_text: The bank shall put in place a cyber/information security organization responsible for designing, establishing, operating and improving cyber security/information security program. These shall consider leading industry practices.
controls.category: Cyber security policy and the organization

controls.title: Minimum contents of the security program
controls.description: The security program shall cover policies, roles & accountability, control framework, asset classification & ownership, risk assessments, security in all processes, incident monitoring, IAM, performance metrics and awareness.
controls.full_text: The security program shall include, but not limited to the following: Development and ongoing maintenance of security policies; Assignment of roles, responsibilities and accountability for information security; Development/maintenance of a security and control framework that consists of standards, measures, practices and procedures; Classification and assignment of ownership of information assets; Periodic risk assessments and ensuring adequate, effective and tested controls for people, processes and technology to enhance information security; Ensuring security is integral to all organizational processes; Processes to monitor security incidents; Effective identity and access management processes; Generation of meaningful metrics of security performance; Information security related awareness sessions to users/officials, including senior officials and board members.
controls.category: Cyber security policy and the organization

controls.title: Board-approved cyber strategy policy
controls.description: Bank must put in place a policy defining strategy and approach to address cyber threats given complexity and risk appetite; board-approved.
controls.full_text: The bank must put in place a policy, that clearly defines the strategy and documents the approach to address cyber threats given the level of complexity of business and acceptable levels of risk; and this must be duly approved by their board. It should highlight the risks from cyber threats and the measures to be taken to address/mitigate these risks.
controls.category: Cyber security policy and the organization
evidence_requirements: Mapping of risks to mitigating measures

controls.title: Segregation of Information Security Group from IT
controls.description: Bank shall form a separate Information Security function/group with segregation of duties from the IT division that implements IT requirements.
controls.full_text: The bank shall form a separate Information Security function/group (team, committee, etc.) to focus exclusively on information/cyber security. There must be segregation of duties between the Information Security Group and the IT division which actually implements the IT requirements.
controls.category: Cyber security policy and the organization
evidence_requirements: Organisation chart showing SoD between Infosec and IT

controls.title: Information Security Group sized to bank's activities
controls.description: Information Security Group shall address the requirements of the bank considering the size and nature of activities.
controls.full_text: The Information Security Group shall be able to address the requirements of the bank considering the size and nature of activities (such as banking and delivery channels).
controls.category: Cyber security policy and the organization

controls.title: CISO appointment and independent reporting line
controls.description: Bank must appoint a CISO reporting to an independent governing body, not the IT head/CIO/CTO, with working relationship to CIO/CTO.
controls.full_text: The bank must appoint a Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), responsible for the Information Security Group. The CISO must report to an independent governing body and shall not have a direct relationship with the IT head/ Chief Information Officer (CIO)/Chief Technology Officer (CTO). CISO must have a working relationship with the CIO/CTO to understand IT infrastructure and operations, to build effective cyber security across the bank, in line with business requirements and objectives.
controls.category: Cyber security policy and the organization
evidence_requirements: Job description showing independence from CIO/CTO

controls.title: Security forum facilitated by CISO
controls.description: Bank shall form a security forum with CEO, CFO, business unit executives, CIO/IT head, HR, Legal, Risk, Audit, Operations, PR - facilitated by the CISO.
controls.full_text: The bank shall form a security forum comprising of responsible parties from various functions, such as the Chief Executive Officer (CEO); Chief Financial Officer (CFO); business unit executives; the CIO/IT head, heads of HR, Legal, Risk Management, Audit, Operations and Public Relations. The forum meetings shall be facilitated by the CISO.
controls.category: Cyber security policy and the organization

controls.title: Information Security Committee responsibilities
controls.description: Information Security Committee shall review/implement policies, approve major projects/budgets, support ISMP, review incidents/assessments, monitor awareness, assess new developments, report to the board.
controls.full_text: The Information Security Committee shall be responsible for the following activities, including but not limited to: Reviewing and facilitating the implementation of information security policies, standards and procedures to ensure that all the risks are managed within the bank's cyber risk appetite. Approving and monitoring major information security projects and the status of information security plans and budgets, establishing priorities, approving standards and procedures. Supporting the review and implementation of a bank-wide Information Security Management Program. Reviewing security incidents, information security assessments and monitoring activities across the bank. Reviewing the status of the security awareness program. Assessing new developments or issues relating to information security. Reporting to the board of directors on information security activities.
controls.category: Cyber security policy and the organization

controls.title: Adequate resourcing of Information Security Group
controls.description: Information Security Group shall be adequately resourced (people, skills, tools for risk assessment, security architecture, VA, forensics).
controls.full_text: The Information Security Group shall be adequately resourced in terms of number of staff members, level of skills and tools or techniques, such as risk assessment, security architecture, vulnerability assessment and forensic assessment.
controls.category: Cyber security policy and the organization

controls.title: CISO responsibilities
controls.description: Defines CISO responsibilities covering security plans, technical security advice, system security standards, audit/log review, programme presentation, security architecture, personnel management, risk assessments, awareness, threat/vulnerability identification, and critical infrastructure protection.
controls.full_text: It must be ensured that the CISO has the following responsibilities: Ensuring the development, maintenance, updating and implementation of security risk management plans, system security plans and any security procedures used. Providing technical security advice regarding system development, acquisition, implementation, modification, operation, support and architecture. Assisting the system manager to develop system security standards/policies. Performing regular review of system security, system audit trails and logs and the integrity of system configurations. Presenting and justifying the information security program and related framework(s) to the CEO, and maintaining a dedicated budget. Developing a security architecture that is in line with the business strategy. Managing other levels of personnel who implement the security architecture and perform information security duties. Performing risk assessments that will validate the security architecture and uncover flaws that need attention. Communicating the security policy, practices and procedures, as well as managing a security awareness program. Identifying potential threats and vulnerabilities, in order to formulate proper information security techniques to counter them. Ensuring appropriate organizational involvement in the critical infrastructure protection efforts for the countries where the organization does business.
controls.category: Cyber security policy and the organization
evidence_requirements: CISO job description covering all listed responsibilities

controls.title: Cyber resilience indicators
controls.description: Bank shall have cyber resilience capabilities assessed and measured through development of indicators.
controls.full_text: The bank shall have cyber resilience capabilities assessed and measured through the development of indicators to assess the level of preparedness/risks.

controls.title: Independent compliance checks/audits of indicators
controls.description: Indicators shall be assessed through independent compliance checks/audits carried out by qualified competent professionals.
controls.full_text: These indicators shall be assessed through independent compliance checks/audits carried out by qualified and competent professionals.

controls.title: Semi-annual board monitoring of indicators
controls.description: Board shall periodically (at least semi-annually) monitor cyber security key indicators with remedial action plans for any deviations. Indicators cover risks (coverage, top risks); compliance (external, internal, readiness); incidents (statistics, mgmt); awareness (learning scores, training coverage, awareness-related incidents); threat level (external, internal); key cyber projects (impact on risk reduction, progress).
controls.full_text: The board shall periodically (at least semi-annually) monitor cyber security key indicators. Senior management shall put in place a remedial action plan to address the deviations, if any. The cyber security indicators are shown below: Risks: coverage; top risks. Compliance: external; internal; readiness. Incidents: statistics; incident management. Awareness and culture: learning scores; training coverage; incidents and other violations associated with awareness. Threat level: external; internal. Key cyber security projects in progress: impact on risk reduction; progress.

controls.title: HR policies aligned to Information Security Policy
controls.description: Bank shall define HR policies and processes in line with the Information Security Policy; document infosec responsibilities for employees, third parties and contractors.
controls.full_text: The bank shall define HR policies and processes in line with the organization's Information Security Policy. HR policies shall document information security responsibilities for employees, third party and contractors.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Human Resources (HR) department

controls.title: Infosec responsibilities in role descriptions
controls.description: Information security responsibilities shall be part of role responsibilities and job descriptions, monitored throughout employment.
controls.full_text: Information security responsibilities shall be included as part of the employees' role responsibilities and job descriptions. These responsibilities should be monitored throughout an individual's employment.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Human Resources (HR) department
evidence_requirements: Sample job descriptions with infosec sections
Performance review templates including infosec objectives

controls.title: HR policies available and known to staff
controls.description: HR policies shall be available to all staff; ensure employees are aware of and comply with policies and infosec obligations.
controls.full_text: HR policies shall be made available to all staff. It must be ensured that employees are aware of, and comply with, policies and their obligations to information security.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Human Resources (HR) department

controls.title: Disciplinary process for security violations
controls.description: Define and enforce a disciplinary process as part of HR policy; ensure employees are aware of it.
controls.full_text: The bank must define a disciplinary process as a part of HR policy. It shall be ensured that the process is enforced and the employees are aware of it.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Human Resources (HR) department

controls.title: Terms, conditions and NDAs at joining/role change
controls.description: Employees, contractors and third party staff shall sign terms & conditions and confidentiality/NDA when joining or on change of job profile.
controls.full_text: The bank shall ensure that all employees, contractors and third party staff sign terms and conditions, as well as a confidentiality and non-disclosure agreement when joining, or in the event of a change of job profile.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Human Resources (HR) department

controls.title: Handling of personally identifiable information
controls.description: Handle personnel PII with due care/diligence in line with the Information Privacy and Protection Law.
controls.full_text: The bank shall handle personally identifiable information, collected from personnel with due care and diligence, in line with requirements for handling personal information specified by Information Privacy and Protection Law.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Human Resources (HR) department
evidence_requirements: Privacy impact assessment for HR data

controls.title: Visitor controls for vendors, contractors and guests
controls.description: Visitors shall be logged with unique identifiable info, issued visitor badge, wear noticeable Visitor sign, made aware of policy obligations, and escorted in secure areas.
controls.full_text: The bank must ensure that vendors, contractors, delegates or guests visiting bank's premises are: Logged with unique identifiable information including date, time and purpose of admittance. Provided with a visitor badge or identification tag. Wearing a noticeable sign displaying their status as 'Visitor' at all times. Made aware of their obligations in compliance with the security policies of the bank. Escorted by the bank's employees while accessing secure areas.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Human Resources (HR) department

controls.title: HR change request on duty change/termination
controls.description: HR shall generate a change request when an employee/contractor/3P has a duty change or termination, ensuring asset return and access amendment/removal.
controls.full_text: The bank must ensure that a change request from the HR department is generated when there is a change of: Duties or termination of contract of an employee, contractor or third party occurs, ensuring that employees, contractors and third parties return bank's physical and logical assets. Access are amended/removed as appropriate.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Human Resources (HR) department

controls.title: Least privilege / need-to-have user rights
controls.description: User rights shall be restricted to the minimum needed to fulfil job requirements per least-privilege and need-to-have principles.
controls.full_text: The bank shall ensure that user rights are restricted to the minimum of information an individual will need to fulfill their job requirements, as per least privilege and need to have principles.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Human Resources (HR) department

controls.title: Controls preventing unauthorised disclosure or misuse
controls.description: Implement adequate controls to prevent employees, vendors, contractors and visitors from making unauthorised disclosures or misusing/corrupting information.
controls.full_text: The bank shall implement adequate controls to prevent employees, vendors, contractors and visitors from making unauthorized disclosures, misusing or corrupting information, as per the bank's security policies.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Human Resources (HR) department

controls.title: Insider risk exposure considered in risk assessment
controls.description: Risk assessment shall consider internal user risks including altering/deleting data, disrupting systems, misuse, holding data hostage, and data theft for espionage or fraud.
controls.full_text: The bank should consider risk exposures from internal users, including altering data; deleting production and back-up data; disrupting/destroying systems; misusing systems for personal gain or to damage the bank; holding data hostage and stealing strategic or customer data for espionage or fraud schemes, as part of its risk assessment process.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Human Resources (HR) department

controls.title: Security awareness program with budget
controls.description: Establish a security awareness program and allocate adequate budget for initiation, execution and maintenance.
controls.full_text: The bank shall establish a security awareness program and allocate adequate budget for initiation, execution and maintenance of the program.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Human Resources (HR) department

controls.title: Annual review/update of awareness content
controls.description: Awareness content shall be reviewed and updated at least annually to reflect new trends, threats, IT changes, and applicable laws/regulations.
controls.full_text: Content of security training and awareness shall be reviewed and updated at least annually to reflect new trends, new threats and changes in bank IT systems, and applicable laws and regulations.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Human Resources (HR) department

controls.title: Awareness material content
controls.description: Training material shall include security requirements, legal/regulatory requirements, business processes/controls, enforcement, incident reporting contacts and acceptable usage including customer information, cyber risks and protections.
controls.full_text: The training program material shall include bank's security requirements; legal and regulatory requirements; business specific processes and controls; enforcement and disciplinary process; contact information for reporting security incidents, as well as the acceptable usage of information processing systems, including customer information educating them about cyber security risks and the protection measures at their level.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Human Resources (HR) department

controls.title: Availability of policies/standards/procedures to staff
controls.description: Training material and IT security policies/standards/procedures shall be available electronically or in hard copy to all employees and relevant long-term onsite vendors/contractors.
controls.full_text: Security training material, IT Security policies, standards and procedures shall be made available, either electronically or in hard copy, to all bank employees and any relevant long-term onsite vendors/contractors acting in the same capacity as staff.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Human Resources (HR) department
evidence_requirements: Intranet/LMS access for staff and onsite vendors

controls.title: Role-appropriate training for staff and third parties
controls.description: Provide appropriate training regarding bank's policies and procedures relevant to job function, role, responsibilities and skills.
controls.full_text: All employees of the bank, contractors and third party (long term or may be acting as staff) shall be provided with appropriate training regarding the bank's policies and procedures, as relevant for their job function, roles, responsibilities and skills.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Human Resources (HR) department

controls.title: Induction and annual refresher with social engineering awareness
controls.description: Provide infosec awareness during induction; conduct annual refresher; train staff to recognise social engineering and not to disclose information that could violate policy.
controls.full_text: The bank must provide the Information Security awareness training to the new employees as part of the wider induction program. Refresher training must be conducted on an annual basis at least. Employees shall be trained to recognize social engineering attempts and to not disclose any information that could violate the bank's policy.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Human Resources (HR) department

controls.title: Post-training assessment and senior/board awareness
controls.description: Assess training effectiveness; maintain attendance and acknowledgement; ensure organisation-wide commitment; provide nuanced cyber threat sessions to senior management and board.
controls.full_text: The bank shall perform an assessment following the training to ascertain the effectiveness of the training program. The attendance records of the security awareness training programs along with the employee's acknowledgement of having received and understood the training, should be maintained. The bank shall ensure the commitment of the entire organization in managing cyber risks, and ensure awareness among staff at all levels. Senior management and board members shall be made aware of the nuances of cyber threats through appropriate training sessions.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Human Resources (HR) department

controls.title: Awareness across stakeholders (customers, vendors, partners)
controls.description: Promote understanding of cyber resilience objectives among customers, vendors, service providers and other stakeholders; ensure measures so they support security preparedness.
controls.full_text: The bank shall actively promote, among their customers, vendors, service providers and other relevant stakeholders, an understanding of bank's cyber resilience objectives, and require and ensure appropriate action to support their synchronized implementation and testing. Measures shall be taken to ensure that all the relevant stakeholders are aware of the potential impact of a cyber-attack and that they play a role in supporting the security preparedness of the bank.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Human Resources (HR) department

controls.title: Training awareness program characteristics
controls.description: Awareness program shall focus on blockable hacker methods, update annually, mandate annual completion, monitor for completion, and deliver via online or classroom training.
controls.full_text: The bank shall consider implementing a training awareness program to ensure security awareness: Focuses only on the methods used by hacker for intrusions which can be blocked through individual action. Is updated on annual basis to represent the latest attack techniques. Is mandated for completion by all employees on an annual basis at minimum. Is monitored for employee completion. The bank shall opt to deliver the training through a computer based online training or class room based session.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Human Resources (HR) department
evidence_requirements: Course catalogue mapping to attack techniques

controls.title: Information security and governance program for legal/compliance requirements
controls.description: Ensure an information security and governance program is in place to address legal and compliance requirements pertaining to cyber security.
controls.full_text: The bank shall ensure that an information security and governance program is in place to address legal and compliance requirements pertaining to cyber security.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Legal and Compliance department

controls.title: Comply with current and future laws/regulations
controls.description: Comply with relevant current provisions of laws and regulations and those which may be amended or added in future.
controls.full_text: The bank shall comply with relevant current provisions of laws and regulations, and those which may be amended and added at a later date in time.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Legal and Compliance department

controls.title: Annual audit of information systems
controls.description: Audit of information systems (infrastructure, people, processes) at least annually or on changes impacting security; fix non-conformances within defined timelines.
controls.full_text: The bank shall ensure that an audit of its information systems (infrastructure, people and processes) is carried out at least once every year, or whenever it undergoes a change that may impact the security of the bank. The scope of the audit process shall include all information assets, people and processes. It shall be ensured that all non-conformance highlighted in audit/assessment are fixed within defined timelines.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Legal and Compliance department

controls.title: Reassessment on change or new findings
controls.description: Reassess where change or new finding invalidates or questions current assessment; full reassessment for major design-affecting changes.
controls.full_text: The bank shall carry out a reassessment where any change or new finding invalidates or questions the current assessment. Full reassessment shall be carried out for major changes affecting the basic security design of a system.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Legal and Compliance department

controls.title: Audit coverage and exemption process
controls.description: All infrastructure, people and processes shall be in audit scope; exemptions require case to QCB defining scope, reason, risk analysis and approvals.
controls.full_text: The bank shall ensure that all infrastructure, people and processes are part of the audit. If an exemption is needed, a case shall be presented to the QCB/authority designated by QCB, defining scope of exemption, reason for exemption, risk analysis of exception and approval from the relevant head of department and the Risk department.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Legal and Compliance department
evidence_requirements: Exemption case files with QCB notification

controls.title: Organisational structure for legal/compliance enforcement
controls.description: Define organisational structure for legal/compliance enforcement: Board-level Risk Mgmt Forum identifies/addresses legal risks; legal function advises business on IT-arising legal issues; Operational Risk Group addresses legal risks under ORM framework.
controls.full_text: The bank shall put in place a well-defined organizational structure for addressing legal and compliance enforcement across the bank. The Risk Management Forum at board-level needs to put processes in place to ensure that legal risks arising from cyber laws are identified and addressed. The forum must ensure that the concerned functions are adequately staffed and that the HR members are trained to carry out all relevant tasks. The bank must establish a legal function to advise the business groups on the legal issues arising out of use of IT with respect to the legal risk identified and referred to it by the Operational Risk Group. The Operational Risk Group must be established to address legal risks as part of an operational risk framework, and take steps to mitigate the risks involved in consultation with the bank's legal functions.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Legal and Compliance department

controls.title: Periodic communication of legal risks; legal instruments coverage
controls.description: Communicate legal risks to senior mgmt and Risk Mgmt Forum incorporating at minimum: applicable legislation identification, IPR, protection of records, data protection/privacy, regulation of cryptographic controls.
controls.full_text: Legal risks shall be periodically communicated to the senior management and board/Risk Management Forum of the board. This shall be enforced by incorporating at a minimum the legal instruments listed below: Identification of applicable legislation - all relevant statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements, and the bank's approach to meet these requirements shall be explicitly defined, documented, and kept up to date for each information system. Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) - appropriate procedures shall be implemented to ensure compliance with legislative, regulatory, and contractual requirements on the use of material in respect to IPR and on the use of proprietary software products. Protection of organizational records - important records shall be protected from loss, destruction and falsification, in accordance with statutory, regulatory, contractual and business requirements. Data protection and privacy of personal information - data protection and privacy shall be ensured as required in relevant legislation, regulations and, if applicable, contractual clauses. Regulation of cryptographic controls - cryptographic controls shall be used in compliance with all relevant agreements, laws and regulations.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Legal and Compliance department
evidence_requirements: Legal risk report to senior mgmt/board

controls.title: PCI-DSS and PA-DSS compliance
controls.description: Comply with Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI-DSS) and Payment Application Data Security Standard (PA-DSS).
controls.full_text: The bank shall comply with Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI-DSS) and Payment Application Data Security Standard (PCA-DSS) standard.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Legal and Compliance department

controls.title: Audit charter/policy for internal audit
controls.description: Prepare audit charter/policy with mandate, purpose, responsibility, accountability, member authority for IS audit; reference SLAs for unplanned work, reports, costs, grievance redressal, quality, performance review, communication, needs assessment, control risk self-assessment, ToR, reporting and findings agreement.
controls.full_text: The bank shall prepare an audit charter or policy to guide the internal audit function. The charter shall contain a clear description of its mandate, purpose, responsibility, accountability and authority of members in respect of an Information Security (IS) audit, namely the IS auditor, management and Audit Committee. Additionally, it must include relevant references to service-level agreements for aspects such as availability for unplanned work; delivery of reports; costs; grievance redressal; quality of service; review of performance; communication with the auditee; needs assessment; control risk self-assessment; agreement of Terms of Reference (ToR) for audit, reporting process and agreement of findings.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Legal and Compliance department

controls.title: Structured audit program for IT risks
controls.description: Establish well-planned structured audit program to evaluate risk management practices, internal controls and policy compliance for IT risks; consider risk-based internal audit covering risk assessment, IS audit planning, audit universe/scope, execution, evidence and documentation.
controls.full_text: It shall be ensured that a well-planned, structured audit program is established to evaluate risk management practices, internal controls systems and compliance with policies concerning IT related risks. To achieve this, the bank must consider risk based internal audit and shall include understanding of IT risk assessment, IS audit planning, defining audit universe and scope of audit, execution, evidence of audit and documentation of audit.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Legal and Compliance department

controls.title: Independence and objectivity of IT/security audit
controls.description: Audit charter/policy/engagement letter shall address independence; impairments disclosed to AC/board; independence regularly assessed; rotation from IT to IS audit managed; follow-up and escalation processes.
controls.full_text: The bank shall establish an organizational structure and reporting lines for IT and security audit in a way that preserves the independence and objectivity of the audit function. The audit charter or policy, or engagement letter (in case of external professional service provider), must address independence and accountability of the Audit function. In case independence is impaired (in fact or appearance), details of the impairment shall be disclosed to the Audit Committee or board. Independence must be regularly assessed by the Audit Committee. In case of rotation of audit staff members from IT department to the IS Audit, care must be taken to ensure that the previous role of such individuals does not impact their independence and objectivity as an IS auditor. A follow-up process to track and monitor IT audit issues, as well as an escalation process to notify the relevant IT and business management of key IT audit issues, must be established.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Legal and Compliance department

controls.title: Risk-based audit cycle frequency
controls.description: Establish risk-based audit cycle: very high to high risk apps 6-12 months, medium 18 months or below, low up to 36 months; cycles must not be open-ended.
controls.full_text: The bank must establish an audit cycle that determines the frequency of IT audits. The audit frequency should be commensurate with the criticality and risk of the IT system or process. The maximum length for audit cycles, based on the risk assessment process for 'very high' to 'high risk' applications, can be at a frequency ranging from 6 to 12 months, medium risk applications can be 18 months (or below) and up to 36 months for low-risk areas. Audit cycles should not be open-ended.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Legal and Compliance department

controls.title: Annual legal-risk impact assessment of cyber incidents
controls.description: Perform impact assessment of legal risks arising from cyber security incidents at least annually considering data breach, shareholder/customer/supplier litigation; board approves remedial actions.
controls.full_text: The bank shall perform an impact assessment due to legal risks arising from cyber security incidents at least annually. This must consider impact in the event there is a data breach, litigation from shareholders, customers and suppliers. The legal risks must be discussed and remedial actions must be approved by the board.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Legal and Compliance department

controls.title: Application control audit with data integrity focus
controls.description: Include application control audit in a risk-based manner as part of regular internal audit, with focus on data integrity.
controls.full_text: The bank shall include application control audit in a risk based manner as part of regular internal audit with a focus on data integrity.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Legal and Compliance department

controls.title: Risk assessment methodology for internal audit
controls.description: Define and follow a suitable risk assessment methodology covering audit scoping, execution, sampling, analysis, resource mgmt, documentation, CAATs, reporting, escalation, communication and quality assurance.
controls.full_text: The bank shall define, adopt and follow a suitable risk assessment methodology which is in line with the focus on risks to be addressed as a part of the overall internal audit strategy. The methodology must detail upon audit scoping, execution, sample collection, analysis, resource management, documentation requirements, use of computer assisted audit techniques, reporting, escalation measures, communication guidelines, quality review and assurance.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Legal and Compliance department

controls.title: Procurement policy with vendor selection and cyber requirements
controls.description: Define procurement policy for hardware, software and consulting services with vendor selection criteria and contractual/cyber security requirements.
controls.full_text: The bank shall define procurement policy for procurement of hardware, software assets and consulting services from a third party. The policy shall include guidelines and criteria to select vendors or service providers, contractual and cyber security requirements.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Procurement department

controls.title: Vendor evaluation with ethical conduct and due diligence
controls.description: At procurement initiation, assess vendor and evaluate controls including reliability and technology risk; select on evaluation criteria with ethical conduct and due diligence.
controls.full_text: The bank, at the time of initiation of the procurement process, shall assess the vendor and evaluate whether controls are in place, such as ensuring the reliability of the third party company and that the technology chosen will not pose a risk to the business. The vendors shall be selected based on evaluation criteria with ethical conduct and due diligence.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Procurement department

controls.title: Confidentiality, cyber security and right-to-audit clauses
controls.description: Vendor contracts shall include clauses on confidentiality, cyber security and right to audit; responsibilities, obligations, liabilities, bank policies, and applicable standards e.g. PCI DSS for payment systems.
controls.full_text: The bank shall ensure that the contract with vendors includes clauses related to confidentiality, cyber security and right to audit. The agreements shall also clearly mention responsibilities, obligations and liabilities, bank policies, reference to standards to which vendors need to comply such as PCI DSS compliance for payment systems.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Procurement department
evidence_requirements: Sample vendor contracts with required clauses

controls.title: Inheriting bank's security controls to vendors
controls.description: Security controls applying to bank must apply to vendors engaged as contractors, with inheritance highlighted in any third-party agreement.
controls.full_text: Security controls and provisions that apply to a bank must apply to vendors the bank engages as contractors, so that policies and regulations are inherited and shall be highlighted in any third party agreement.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Procurement department
evidence_requirements: Mapping of bank controls to vendor obligations in contracts

controls.title: Annual independent vendor audits or self-assessment
controls.description: Conduct independent vendor audits annually (especially with access to premises/systems) or obtain and evaluate a vendor self-security assessment report.
controls.full_text: The bank shall conduct independent audits of the vendors especially if a vendor has access to bank premises and systems on an annual basis at least, or a self-security assessment report shall be obtained from the vendors and evaluated.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Procurement department

controls.title: Hardening of vendor devices and equipment
controls.description: Vendor devices and equipment must be hardened per hardening guidelines and internal checklists to remove default and insecure configurations.
controls.full_text: Vendor devices and equipment must be hardened as per the hardening guidelines and internal checklists to ensure that default and insecure configurations are removed from the devices.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Procurement department

controls.title: Technology risk management framework
controls.description: Define and establish a technology risk management framework covering roles & responsibilities, asset identification & classification, impact/likelihood/threat/risk/vulnerability identification, plan with policies/procedures/best practices, implementation & regular testing, and monitoring with regular plan updates.
controls.full_text: The bank shall define and establish a risk management framework to manage technology risk. The framework should encompass the following: roles and responsibilities in managing technology risks; identification and classification of assets; identification and assessment of impact and likelihood threat, risk and vulnerabilities on bank systems and operations; development of a plan that contain policies, procedures and best practices that address risks; implement and regular testing of the plan; monitoring of risks and regular update of the plan to take into account the evolution of technologies, legal requirements and other mandatory requirements.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Risk department

controls.title: Periodic effectiveness testing of risk management/internal controls
controls.description: Procedures shall be in place to periodically test effectiveness of risk management practices and internal controls; monitor implemented controls to ensure desired risk mitigation.
controls.full_text: The bank shall ensure that procedures are in place to test the effectiveness of risk management practices and internal controls on periodic basis. The implemented controls shall be monitored to ensure that the desired level of risk mitigation is achieved.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Risk department

controls.title: Information Asset Protection Policy
controls.description: Establish an Information Asset Protection Policy to identify and ascertain asset criticality and develop appropriate protective controls.
controls.full_text: The bank shall establish an Information Asset Protection Policy, to ensure that the criticality of information system assets are identified and ascertained in order to develop appropriate controls to protect them.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Risk department

controls.title: Detailed asset inventory and classification
controls.description: Prepare detailed inventory of information assets and classify by sensitivity; keep up-to-date including business info, customer info, business applications, supporting IT infrastructure, facilities, key personnel, services with business criticality.
controls.full_text: The bank shall prepare a detailed inventory of information assets and classify the assets based on the information classification/sensitivity criteria. The assets inventory shall be kept up-to-date and include business information, customer information, business applications, supporting IT infrastructure and facilities hardware/software/network devices, key personnel, services etc. indicating their business criticality.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Risk department

controls.title: Inventory record fields
controls.description: Asset inventory record shall include clear identification of asset, location, security/risk classification, asset group and its owner, designated custodian.
controls.full_text: The inventory record of the assets shall include the following: clear identification of asset; location; security/risk classification; asset group and its owner; designated custodian.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Risk department

controls.title: Risk assessment process aligned to leading practices
controls.description: Define a risk assessment process and methodology covering internal/external networks, hardware, software, applications, system interfaces, operations and human elements aligned to leading practices.
controls.full_text: The bank shall define a risk assessment process to identify threats and vulnerabilities to bank's environment and information assets, which comprises of internal and external networks, hardware, software, applications, system interfaces, operations and human elements. The bank shall define a risk assessment methodology/risk assessment process aligned to leading practices.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Risk department

controls.title: Impact analysis and quantification
controls.description: Following risk identification, analyse and quantify potential impact and consequences on business and operations.
controls.full_text: Following the risk identification, as per the risk assessment process, the bank shall perform an analysis and quantification of the potential impact and consequences of these risks on business and operations.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Risk department

controls.title: Threat and vulnerability matrix
controls.description: Develop a threat and vulnerability matrix including cyber security threats to assess impact and prioritise risks.
controls.full_text: The bank shall develop a threat and vulnerability matrix, which includes cyber security threats, to assess the impact of threat to its environment. The matrix will help the bank in prioritizing the risks.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Risk department

controls.title: Threat register with cyber threats
controls.description: Threat register shall include DDoS, internal sabotage, malware infestation and other cyber threats; bank shall monitor such risks as a crucial containment step.
controls.full_text: Security threats such as denial of service attacks, internal sabotage, malware infestation and other cyber security threats shall be a part of a threat register. The bank shall monitor such risks, as it is a crucial step in the risk containment exercise.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Risk department

controls.title: Risk appetite definition
controls.description: Risk assessment process shall define the risk appetite as the defined level of risk acceptable by the bank.
controls.full_text: The risk assessment process shall define the risk appetite. Risk appetite is the defined level of risk that may be accepted by the bank.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Risk department

controls.title: Risk treatment plan with avoid/transfer/mitigate/accept
controls.description: Define risk treatment plan; residual risks with aggregate high level shall be vetted by senior management; strategies include avoid, transfer, mitigate, accept.
controls.full_text: Based on the risk assessment, the bank shall define a risk treatment plan to address the threats and vulnerabilities. The risk treatment plan and residual risk selected for information assets, with an aggregate level of high, shall be vetted by the senior management in the bank. Following risk mitigation and control strategies should be considered: Avoid risk: It may be prudent to avoid risks altogether due to its inherent nature. For example, modify or terminate the process that induces risk. Transfer risk: In some cases, it may be advisable to transfer the risk to another entity. For example transfer risk by insurance. Mitigate risk: It is not possible, most of the time, to avoid or transfer the risk. In such cases, it is necessary to reduce the risk to an acceptable level by implementing controls. Accept risk: Even after applying controls, the risk may still not be reduced to an acceptable level; in such cases, a bank may decide if they are prepared to accept the risk.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Risk department
evidence_requirements: Senior management sign-off for high residual risks

controls.title: Integration of risk assessment within business processes
controls.description: Integrate risk assessment within business processes; revise when business environment or legal/regulatory requirements change.
controls.full_text: Risk assessment shall be integrated within business processes and revised whenever there are changes in the business environment or legal/regulatory requirements. Whenever there is a change in business environment, risk assessment must be performed to ensure that changes are aligned to the risk appetite.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Risk department

controls.title: Effectiveness assessment of controls under changed scenarios
controls.description: Effective procedure to assess control effectiveness ensuring controls remain effective in changed scenarios and meet new challenges.
controls.full_text: The bank shall ensure that an effective procedure is in place to assess the effectiveness of the implemented controls. The process shall ensure that implemented controls remain effective in the changed scenarios and are able to meet the new challenges.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Risk department

controls.title: Risk register with periodic review
controls.description: Maintain a risk register facilitating monitoring and reporting; highest-priority risks monitored closely with regular reporting on mitigation actions; reviewed and updated periodically.
controls.full_text: The bank shall maintain a risk register which facilitates monitoring and reporting risks. Risks with the highest priority should be monitored closely, with regular reporting on actions taken to mitigate them. The risk register shall be reviewed and updated periodically.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Risk department

controls.title: Risk matrix highlighting top exposures
controls.description: Develop a risk matrix highlighting systems, processes or infrastructure with highest risk exposure considering risk events, regulatory requirements and audit observations.
controls.full_text: To facilitate risk reporting, the bank shall develop a risk matrix to highlight systems, processes or infrastructure with the highest risk exposure. The bank shall consider risk events, regulatory requirements and audit observations when determining risk matrices.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Risk department
evidence_requirements: Inputs from incidents, audits and regulatory observations

controls.title: Threat intelligence feeds (internal & external)
controls.description: Consider various threat intelligence feeds from internal and external sources to put in place risk mitigation measures for new and evolving risks.
controls.full_text: The bank must consider various threat intelligence feeds, both from internal and external sources, to ensure that risk mitigation measures for the new and evolving risks are put in place.
controls.domain: Cyber security in the Risk department

controls.title: Compliance with QCB BCM Circular and ISO 22301 alignment
controls.description: Comply with QCB BCM Circular Part (VII) Section Eleventh; formulate BCM policy/procedures/plans in line with ISO 22301 and keep updated with latest standards.
controls.full_text: The bank must ensure compliance to the QCB BCM Circular Part (VII) - Instructions of Supervision and Control Section Eleventh: Business Continuity. Additionally, the BCM policy, procedures and plans shall be formulated in line with a global standard such as ISO 22301, and it must be updated with the latest standards.

controls.title: Emergency response plan
controls.description: Formulate an emergency response plan detailing evacuation procedures, command center operations, media and communications strategy.
controls.full_text: The bank must formulate an emergency response plan that details evacuation procedures, command center operations, media and communications strategy.

controls.title: Threat scenario identification and incident management
controls.description: Identify natural and man-made (including cyber) threat scenarios and put in place incident management procedures.
controls.full_text: At a minimum, the banks must identify threat scenarios, natural and man-made (including cyber) and put in place incident management procedures.

controls.title: Head of BCM function responsibilities
controls.description: Appoint senior official as head of BCM function responsible for BCM plan creation, regular updates from business model changes/audit recommendations/BCM drills, ensuring BIA/risk assessment/monitoring/testing annually, and advising senior management on crisis declaration with defined crisis management plan.
controls.full_text: A senior management official must be appointed and designated by the bank as head of the BCM function (team, committee, etc.), who must be responsible for the following: Creation of a BCM plan that includes necessary planning to include the recovery maintenance of all aspects of the business functions. Regularly updating BCP plans based on changes in business models, audit recommendations and key learnings from BCM drills. Ensure that Business Impact Analysis (BIA), risk assessment, monitoring and testing are performed on at least on an annual basis. The types of testing are defined in Section 6.1.9. Evaluate all factors and advise senior management on declaration of a 'crisis'. A crisis management plan shall be defined and roles and responsibilities communicated to stakeholders.

controls.title: BCM committee with cross-functional senior officials
controls.description: Form committee from IT, HR, Legal, Business and Information Security to exercise, maintain and invoke BCM plans; ensure BCM communication/training/awareness, plan review, budget liaison, recovery/continuity/response team coordination and BCP activation decision-making.
controls.full_text: A committee consisting of senior officials from departments such as IT, HR, Legal, Business and Information Security must be formed to exercise, maintain and invoke BCM plans during drills and crisis situations. Additionally, it must be ensured that they are responsible for the following: BCM communication, training and awareness across organization; review of the BCM plan to ensure its completeness; review and liaise over BCM budgets; coordination of recovery, continuity and response teams, and handling key decision-making; determine BCP activation.

controls.title: BCP teams formation across sites
controls.description: Form teams for various aspects of BCP including incident response, IT, damage assessment, logistics and administrative support at central office, standalone offices and branch level.
controls.full_text: The bank must ensure the formation of teams for various aspects of BCP, such as incident response, IT, damage assessment, logistics and administrative support at central office, standalone offices and at a branch level, as required.

controls.title: Stakeholder communication strategy
controls.description: Formulate strategy for communication with regulators, investors, customers, counterparties, business partners, service providers and media; designate trained media spokesperson; prepare draft press releases/templates; regularly exercise communication drills.
controls.full_text: The bank must formulate a formal strategy for communication with key stakeholders such as regulators, investors, customers, counterparties, business partners, service providers and the media. Activities outlined in the strategy must include: A well trained media relations spokesperson shall be designated by the bank to provide information to stakeholders via communication channels. The bank must prepare draft press releases and communication templates as a part of their BCP. Communication drills must be regularly exercised as a part of BCM drills.

controls.title: Annual BCP testing and external audit
controls.description: Test BCP at least annually; tests scoped by application/business function criticality and bank's role; tests from alternate sites; internal audit assesses testing effectiveness; annual external audit by independent experienced auditor against international practices.
controls.full_text: As an essential component of effective BCM, bank shall test their business continuity plans to evaluate their ability to recover operations in the event of a major disruption. Accordingly, the bank should comply with the following: Testing business continuity plans and strategies, BCM updating should be conducted on at least an annual basis. Tests relating to the nature, scope and frequency shall be determined by the criticality of the applications and business functions, the bank's, role in broader market operations and the material changes in the bank's business. Testing shall identify the need to modify the bank's responsibilities, systems, software, hardware, personnel and the external environment. The test program shall incorporate conducting tests from alternate sites with the relevant systems, devices, and personnel. In addition, testing is also essential for promoting awareness, familiarity and understanding among key personnel of their roles and responsibilities in the event of a major operational disruption. Internal audit shall assess the effectiveness of the bank's testing program, review test results and report their findings to the Audit Committee. External auditing shall be undertaken annually by an independent experienced auditor and should include assessment of the bank's testing programs effectiveness in the view of the recent international practices and standards. The bank must, at minimum, conduct four unplanned BCM drills (at least one hot test and three cold tests) on an annual basis, with only a restricted set of identified personnel being made aware of the drill. The bank shall incorporate test results and key learnings from these drills to tailor their BCP plan. The hot test shall be a full simulation test, where all activities are relocated from the original site to the alternative site (announced or unannounced); all necessary employees, suppliers, the moderator, observers and auditors will participate. The cold test shall be conducted so that certain components of the BCP are tested based on the criticality of the business requirements.
evidence_requirements: Annual BCP test plan and results

controls.title: Annual BCP testing components
controls.description: Annual BCP testing shall include table-top, simulation, technical recovery (with component tests like ATM switch), DR testing in parallel, tests of supplier facilities and services, and complete rehearsals.
controls.full_text: Annual BCP testing shall include the following: Table-top testing - discussing business recovery arrangements using example interruptions. Simulation testing - to train personnel in post incident and crisis management roles. Technical recovery testing - to ensure all information systems can be restored effectively. This may also include component testing which is an in-depth testing of individual components, such as ATM switch testing. DR testing - business operations to be run in parallel from DR site. Tests of supplier facilities and services - to ensure contractor and vendor Service Level Agreements (SLAs) are met, as per contract. Complete rehearsals - to test if the organization, personnel, equipment, facilities and processes can cope with a crisis situation.

controls.title: Annual approved BCP submission to QCB
controls.description: Provide approved BCP copy to QCB annually including summary of BCP results describing status of IT systems, key BCM learnings, and bank's implementation strategy.
controls.full_text: The bank shall provide an approved copy of the BCP to the QCB on annual basis which must include summary of BCP results describing the status of bank IT systems, key BCM learnings and the bank's strategy to implement them.
evidence_requirements: Annual BCP submission to QCB with management approval

controls.title: DR procedures for critical systems with full asset documentation
controls.description: Procedures to ensure recovery of key critical systems, applications and infrastructure; DR plans include full description of IT assets, data, information systems and information flow with recovery mechanisms; key resources/documentation available in crisis aligned to BCP strategy and QCB instructions.
controls.full_text: The bank must have procedures in place to ensure the recovery of key critical systems, applications and its related infrastructure. DR plans and processes should include a full description of bank IT assets, data, information system and information flow, including recovery mechanisms. Key resources and documentations should be rendered available in times of crisis, according to the overall BCP strategy of the bank and QCB instructions.

controls.title: BCP/DR supporting cyber resilience with RTO
controls.description: BCP/DR capabilities must support cyber resilience and enable rapid recovery from cyber-attacks within defined and measured RTO while ensuring process/data security; collaborative, coordinated resilience testing with vendors and partners.
controls.full_text: The bank's BCP/DR capabilities must support the bank's cyber resilience objectives and must enable the bank to recover rapidly from cyber-attacks to safely resume critical operations aligned with defined and measured recovery time objectives (RTO) while ensuring security of processes and data. Additionally, collaborative and coordinated resilience testing must be performed with vendors and partners to ensure the readiness of such capabilities in all interconnected systems and networks.
evidence_requirements: Joint resilience test reports with vendors/partners

controls.title: Cyber Crisis Management Plan (CCMP)
controls.description: Formulate CCMP immediately; CCMP must include detection, response, recovery and containment aspects of cyber attacks.
controls.full_text: As cyber risk is different from many other risks, the traditional BCP/DR arrangements may not be adequate. A Cyber Crisis Management Plan (CCMP) must be immediately formulated by the bank. The CCMP must include the four aspects, i.e. detection, response, recovery and containment of cyber attacks.

controls.title: Preventive/corrective measures against emerging cyber threats and CCMP details
controls.description: Deploy measures to prevent threats and promptly detect intrusions; prepare for zero-day, remote access, targeted attacks; address DDoS, ransomware/cryptoware, malware, spam, spear phishing, vishing, drive-by downloads, browser gateway fraud, password-related frauds; document communication strategies; CCMP includes incident response procedures, severity/type/IOC/method of detection/reporting channels/monitoring periodicity/threat info sharing/expected response and quarantine controls.
controls.full_text: The bank shall deploy measures to prevent threats and cyber-attacks and to promptly detect any cyber intrusions so as to respond/recover/contain the fall out. The bank shall be prepared to face emerging cyber threats such as 'zero day' attacks, remote access threats and targeted attacks. Additionally, the bank shall take necessary preventive and corrective measures in addressing various types of cyber threats, such as DDoS, ransomware/crypto ware, malware, spam, spear phishing, vishing frauds, drive by downloads, browser gateway fraud and password related frauds. In addition to this, communication strategies must be documented to respond to such attacks. The CCMP must include documented incident response procedures, including the roles, responsibilities and response strategies to meet various incident scenarios based on situational awareness and potential/post impact, consistent communication and coordination with stakeholders during response. Additionally, the bank must also provide specialized training to personnel handling incidents, post incident review and periodically test incident response plans. The bank shall implement an effective Incident Response Program approved by the board/senior management. The CCMP must define incident severity, type of incidents, indicators of compromise (IOC), method of detection, incident reporting channels, periodicity of monitoring, collection/sharing of threat information, expected response in each scenario/incident type. Additionally, the bank must establish and implement systems to collect and share threat information from local/national/international sources. Cyber Crisis Management Plan (CCMP) must define controls to quarantine the affected devices and systems.
evidence_requirements: Preventive control inventory mapped to listed threats

controls.title: Effective measures to prevent and detect cyber-attacks
controls.description: Take effective measures to prevent cyber-attacks and promptly detect cyber-intrusions in order to respond, recover and contain the fallout.
controls.full_text: The bank must take effective measures to prevent cyber-attacks and to promptly detect any cyber-intrusions so as to respond/recover/contain the fall out.

controls.title: Restriction of work-from-home for critical functions
controls.description: Work from home should not be considered for employees performing critical functions; if required, high privileged users only with prior approval and as-needed.
controls.full_text: 'Work from home' arrangements should not be considered for employees performing critical functions. However, if required, high privileged users shall only be allowed to connect with prior approval and on an as-needed basis.

controls.title: Annual compliance reporting framework to QCB
controls.description: Prepare a reporting framework based on this circular; submit annual compliance report to QCB.
controls.full_text: The bank shall prepare a reporting framework based on this circular. A compliance report based on this framework shall be submitted to QCB on an annual basis at a minimum.
evidence_requirements: Annual compliance reports submitted to QCB

controls.title: Material gap remediation under board oversight
controls.description: Material control gaps shall be identified, remedial actions initiated under board/board-authorized committee guidance; advisory/recommended gaps require documented action plan shared with QCB and signed by board/board-authorized committee.
controls.full_text: The material gaps in controls shall be identified, and remedial actions taken under the guidance of the board/board authorized committee shall be initiated immediately. Should the advisory and recommended requirements not be met, an action plan to address these shall be documented and shared with QCB. The action plan shall be adequately supported by placing mitigation measures. The report needs to be duly signed by the board/board authorized committee.
evidence_requirements: Board-signed action plans submitted to QCB

controls.title: QCB right to audit
controls.description: QCB reserves the right to audit the bank to ensure compliance to this circular at any point in time.
controls.full_text: QCB reserves the right to audit the bank to ensure compliance to this circular at any point in time.

controls.title: Board-approved exception handling
controls.description: Exceptions to mandatory requirements require suitable business justification approved by board/board-authorized committee.
controls.full_text: In case the bank seeks an exception to any mandatory requirement in this circular, the bank shall provide a suitable business justification for these requirements. These justifications shall be approved by the board/board authorized committee.

controls.title: Change Management Policy and rollback
controls.description: Define Change Management Policy with planned major/maintenance/minor/emergency changes across HW/SW/infrastructure; document all changes with rollback procedures; assess business impact.
controls.full_text: The bank shall define a Change Management Policy and supporting procedures. The policy shall include planned major changes, maintenance and minor changes and emergency or unplanned changes across hardware, software and infrastructure. All changes shall be documented along with 'rollback' procedures and its impact on business shall be assessed before implementing them in bank's environment.

controls.title: Change classification
controls.description: Change Management Policy shall include classification of changes to ensure proper use of resources.
controls.full_text: The Change Management Policy shall also include classification of changes to ensure proper use of resources required to execute a change.

controls.title: Cross-functional Change Management Committee
controls.description: Form cross-functional Change Management Committee with reps from business divisions/functional units, process owners, Information Security and Risk Management.
controls.full_text: A cross functional Change Management Committee shall be formed which include representatives from various business divisions/functional units, process owners, and must include representation from the Information Security and Risk Management functions.

controls.title: Security posture reassessment on impactful changes
controls.description: CMC shall assess whether change requires system reassessment when impacting security posture; risk analysis conducted to keep residual risk acceptable.
controls.full_text: The Change Management Committee shall assess if the system requires reassessment in the event that the change has an impact on the security posture of the bank. Risk analysis shall be conducted as part of a change process to keep residual risk at an acceptable level.

controls.title: UAT and test plan with user sign-off
controls.description: Adequately test impending changes; perform UAT before production; develop documented test plans; obtain explicit user sign-off prior to implementation.
controls.full_text: The bank must adequately test the impending changes and ensure that it is accepted by the stakeholders and users by performing User Acceptance Testing (UAT) prior to migration to production systems. The bank shall develop and document appropriate test plans for impending changes. Explicit sign-off must be obtained from the users on test results prior to implementation of change in the production.

controls.title: Separation of duties between requester and implementer
controls.description: Person requesting the change must not be the same individual implementing it; changes implemented by skilled and competent individuals.
controls.full_text: It must be ensured that the person requesting the change is not the same individual who is implementing the changes, and the changes must be implemented by skilled and competent individuals.

controls.title: Separate dev/test/staging/production environments
controls.description: Separate physical and logical environments for systems development, testing, staging and production must be established and maintained.
controls.full_text: Separate physical and logical environments for systems development, testing, staging and production must be established and maintained.

controls.title: Replicate change to DR environment
controls.description: Post successful production implementation, change shall be replicated in DR system/environment for consistency and resilience.
controls.full_text: Post successful implementation of the change in production environment, the change shall also be replicated in the disaster recovery system/environment for consistency and resilience.

controls.title: Post-implementation documentation updates
controls.description: CMC ensures that post-implementation all related processes and system information is documented and updated.
controls.full_text: The Change Management Committee must ensure that post implementation of the change, all related processes and system related information is documented and updated.

controls.title: Post-implementation verification
controls.description: Verify changes after implementation to confirm objective met and no unexpected side effects.
controls.full_text: Following implementation of the change, verification of the changes shall be carried out to confirm that the change has met its objective, and there have been no unexpected side effects.

controls.title: Logging facility and semi-annual change process review
controls.description: Enable logging facility to record change-process activities; review change management process and classification structure at least every six months.
controls.full_text: The bank should ensure that a logging facility is enabled to record activities that are performed during the change process. It is recommended that the bank reviews the change management process and change classification structure for effective change management at least once every six months.

controls.title: Incident management framework and policy
